title: Abundant Mines plans landfill-powered Bitcoin mine near Mexico City
html:
US Bitcoin mining company Abundant Mines has announced that it is planning to develop a landfill gas-powered cryptomine near Mexico City.

The company is working with methane mitigation investment firm CH4 Capital and Mexico’s Kardashev BTC on the project, which would use gas produced by decomposing waste to generate electricity for mining equipment.

CH4 Capital identifies the site as the Relleno Sanitario Chicoloapan, in Chicoloapan, State of Mexico. The landfill is operated by Grupo Contadero.

The partners have published different capacity figures. In a November 25 LinkedIn article, Abundant Mines co-founder and CEO Beau Turner described an initial 2MW facility with potential to expand to 8MW. CH4 Capital’s project page lists a 4MW first phase and estimates the landfill has enough gas to support 8–10MW in total.

According to Turner, the project targets a landfill where methane currently escapes into the atmosphere, rather than one where the gas is already captured and burned through flaring.

The development would collect and process landfill gas, then feed it into generators supplying electricity to the on-site cryptomine. CH4 Capital says consuming power at the landfill avoids the need for a grid connection or gas pipeline.

CH4 Capital’s operating model also includes a backup flare to burn captured gas when generators are unavailable, alongside continuous measurement of gas flow and methane content.

CH4 Capital finances gas capture, generation, and mining equipment through loans to mining operators. The fund says it earns interest on those loans and income from carbon credits generated by methane destruction, while the miner retains the Bitcoin produced.

All equipment deployed during the Mexican project’s initial phase will be owned and operated by Abundant Mines, Turner said.

“No client-owned miners will be hosted at this location,” he wrote.

The additional capacity is intended to support the company’s Hashrate Redirect program, which allocates computing power from its own fleet to customers whose hosted machines experience qualifying downtime.

Turner said developing landfill-powered sites requires substantial infrastructure and time to optimize gas collection. He described opportunities at locations where supplying electricity to the grid or upgrading gas for other uses is not commercially practical.

CH4 Capital identifies Chicoloapan as its first financed project and says it is pursuing further landfill developments in Mexico and elsewhere in Latin America.

Landfill gas has previously been used to power data center sites as companies seek cheaper and more environmentally friendly ways to power their projects. Earlier this year, DCD reported on UK data center developer Era4 planning a landfill gas-powered data center in Kent.
summary: Project backed by CH4, more Latin landfills targeted
